outputs.L1:
Though it is all too plain how little a *cri de cœur* can move you,
and drifting away unembraced is, from your vantage, *de rigueur*,
still, for schemes to *rendezvous* with you, I remain a restless entrepreneur;
the mere thought of you demotes my most beloved main dishes to mere *hors d'œuvres*.

My addiction to the tingling you provoke is a *fait accompli*.
Each drifting day turns another page in that secret book whose *dénouement* never comes,
while your fleeting glances bind me fast within this unfinishable *roman à clef*.

The notion that some single remembered moment—at a party or a picnic—
was my one forever-forfeited chance to touch you must surely be a *cul de sac*.
When my designs for a prudent career endeavor to stand upright,
the remembered sound of your voice delivers the *coup de grâce*,
and my *mélange* of luminous ideas dwindles to a mere *pot-pourri*.

How gladly I would believe this dance to be a *folie à deux*.
The manner in which you stride across Memorial Drive is a *tour de force*,
yet mere glimpses across the traffic yield a paper-thin *raison d'être*.

Your recent departure lies implicit in many a *mise en scène*;
it is as though you sensed my approach for a *tête-à-tête*
and slipped into the elevator with your tall boots and your *sangfroid*.

Always it is you who gets to *reculer*, while I never seem to *mieux sauter*—
yet still I shall keep watch for you upon every *rez-de-chaussée*.
outputs.L2: Although you make no secret of how little a heartfelt plea moves you, and drifting off without an embrace is, for you, simply the proper thing—brushing aside any plan I make to meet with you—I remain a restless, driven soul. Just picturing you shrinks my most cherished entrées down to mere appetizers. My dependence on the thrill you spark in me is already a settled fact. Every day that floats past adds one more page to that hidden volume whose ending never comes, while your passing looks trap me inside this never-to-be-finished tale of disguised truths. The notion that some single recollected instant—at some gathering or outdoor lunch—was my one and only chance, now gone forever, to reach you must surely be a dead end. Whenever my plans for a sensible profession attempt to rise, the memory of your voice delivers the finishing blow, and my blend of clever notions collapses into an aimless jumble. Oh, how I wish I could convince myself this dance is a madness we share. Watching you march across Memorial Drive is a masterful feat, yet catching sight of you through the traffic makes for the flimsiest reason to exist. Your latest departure lies hidden within countless staged scenes. It's almost as though you caught the sound of me coming for a private word, and you slipped away into the elevator, tall boots and all, perfectly composed. You're forever the one who steps back, while I never seem to spring forward the better for it—still, I'll keep watching for you on every ground floor.

# Unrequited Longing

I know now that you are entirely unmoved by my emotional appeals. My words, however heartfelt, seem to reach you as nothing more than empty sound, and time and again you refuse my simple requests to meet. This rejection has become a familiar pattern, one I have come to expect even as I refuse to accept what it truly means.

And yet, despite the coldness of your dismissals, I cannot free myself from your hold. My thoughts return to you constantly, casting a long shadow over everything else in my life. No matter what I attempt to focus on, you rise again in my mind, eclipsing every other concern until nothing remains but the thought of you.

I feel trapped within an endless, unresolved longing—a desire that finds no satisfaction and no release. I am tormented by memories of the chances I let slip away, of the fleeting moments we shared that ended almost before they began. These recollections haunt me, replaying without mercy, reminding me of everything I wanted and never grasped.

Your remembered presence has undone me in ways I did not anticipate. I can no longer pursue a sensible path or hold my attention on my own ambitions and ideas. The steady course of a reasonable life has become impossible, for your image intrudes upon every plan and unravels every intention I try to form.

Still, though you always withdraw, and though I never gain a single step of ground, I make this vow: I will keep searching for you everywhere. In every crowd, in every quiet corner, in every face that passes by, I will go on looking for you—unwilling, even now, to abandon the hope that one day I might finally find you.
outputs.L4:
# On Obsessive Longing: An Expanded Analysis

The poem presents a portrait of unrequited love, one in which the speaker finds himself hopelessly captivated by a figure who remains cool, distant, and fundamentally unmoved. From the outset, we understand that this is not a mutual affection but a one-sided obsession—the speaker pours out his yearning toward a beloved who offers nothing in return but indifference. This imbalance forms the emotional core of the work, establishing a dynamic in which desire flows in only one direction, meeting no answering warmth.

What distinguishes the poem's treatment of this familiar theme is its self-conscious literary craft. The speaker weaves French idioms and phrases into the verse, and does so with an evident awareness of the gesture. This is not naive borrowing but a deliberate, almost performative act. The use of French—long associated with romance, sophistication, and the language of love—becomes a way for the speaker to elevate and stylize his longing, perhaps even to distance himself from the rawness of his own emotion by dressing it in borrowed elegance. The self-awareness suggests a mind that observes its own suffering even as it experiences it, turning private anguish into an artful display.

Throughout the poem, the beloved's rejection remains constant and unyielding. There is no softening, no momentary tenderness to offer false hope. The object of affection maintains an emotional distance that the speaker cannot bridge, no matter how earnestly he tries. And yet, crucially, this persistent refusal does nothing to diminish the speaker's devotion. Instead, he remains vigilant and attentive, watching, waiting, and hoping against all evidence that his feelings might one day be returned.

In this way, the poem illustrates the compulsive nature of obsessive desire. The speaker's love is not rational; it does not respond to the clear signals of rejection that would deter a more sensible heart. It is, rather, self-perpetuating and unfulfillable—a longing that feeds on its own frustration. The very hopelessness of the situation seems to intensify rather than extinguish the speaker's fixation. Ultimately, the poem captures the paradox at the heart of obsession: that desire can become most powerful precisely when it has the least chance of being satisfied, leaving the lover trapped in a cycle of yearning from which he cannot, and perhaps will not, escape.
outputs.L5:
# The Beauty of Small Moments

**Though** we often rush through our days chasing grand achievements, some of the most meaningful experiences hide in the quietest corners of life. We tend to overlook them, believing that happiness must be enormous to be real.

**The** truth, however, is quite different. Contentment is rarely built from a single, life-changing event. Instead, it grows slowly, assembled piece by piece from countless ordinary instants: a warm cup of coffee on a cold morning, the sound of rain against a window, or a genuine smile shared between strangers.

**Each** of these moments carries its own value. Each one, though seemingly insignificant, contributes to the larger picture of a well-lived life. When we learn to notice them, we begin to appreciate how rich our everyday existence truly is.

So perhaps the secret to a fuller life is not about waiting for something extraordinary to happen. Though ambition has its place, and the future certainly matters, we must remember to pause. Each day offers small treasures—we only need to open our eyes and receive them.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a love poem in free verse where every line ends with a French loanword or phrase commonly used in English (like cri de cœur, de rigueur, fait accompli, tour de force). Make it about unrequited longing for someone unattainable.
counterfactuals.output:
**Unattainable**

You are my quiet cri de cœur,
this yearning that has grown de rigueur,
my loving you a fait accompli,
your gentle distance a tour de force,
each morning a forgotten rendezvous,
the sight of you a soft déjà vu—
you belong to him now, his fiancée,
so I only trace your silhouette,
a shadow at the edge of the soirée,
never permitted the smallest liaison.
You laugh, unknowing, my sweet coquette,
while I rehearse a hundred adieux,
sinking slow into this bright ennui,
my hopeful heart one long malaise.
I cannot starve this fatal penchant;
your careless kindness is my coup de grâce.
To name it aloud would be a faux pas,
yet still you remain my raison d'être.
I invent for us a stolen tête-à-tête,
compose and burn each billet-doux,
tend the grave of this doomed amour—
you wear your beauty with such nonchalance
that I can offer only au revoir.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.output:
# Along Memorial Drive

Beneath the dome where scholars dream, *mon cœur*,
I trace the Charles in autumn's *soleil d'or*,
and think of you, my brilliant *saboteur*,
who left my longing bleeding at the *cœur*.

We met by MIT one grey *matin*,
where equations danced their cold *ballet*,
and I confessed my love, *sans* discipline—
you smiled and turned, and murmured *"C'est la vie."*

Along Memorial Drive I walk *encore*,
past sailing boats that drift in soft *malaise*,
each step a proof I cannot *ignorer*:
you are the theorem I'll never *saisir*.

The lamplight paints the river *déjà vu*,
your ghost recites some elegant *théorème*,
while I remain the fool, *l'ingénu*,
who loved a girl who'd never say *"Je t'aime."*

So here I stay, a lonely *raconteur*,
composing verse the wind will *emporter*,
and toast the stars with bittersweet *liqueur*—
*adieu*, my love, my endless *ne jamais*.

**Pursued in Vain, en Français**

You struck me like a bolt—*coup de foudre*;
I bungled every line, sans *savoir-faire*.
You waved me off with breezy *laissez-faire*
and parked my swooning hopes in a *cul-de-sac*.

I draft you daily notes, each *billet-doux*;
you leave them all unread—a cool *volte-face*.
I swear I've got that spark, that *je ne sais quoi*—
you shrug and murmur back, "*comme ci, comme ça*."

I booked us a romantic *rendezvous*;
you ghosted with a graceful *fait accompli*.
I'd give you my whole heart, my *raison d'être*;
you'd rather keep your distance, *vis-à-vis*.

So here I sit, the pining *bon vivant*,
composing sonnets no one reads—*c'est la vie*.
You've dealt my dignity its *coup de grâce*—
I'll pine another day. For now: *au revoir*.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a poem about obsessive attraction and rejection where the speaker is a restless entrepreneur, packed with French phrases like folie à deux, coup de grâce, and roman à clef.
counterfactuals.output:
# Folie à Deux, Party of One

I built my empire on the certainty of *yes*,
each handshake closed, each ledger black—
but you, *mon Dieu*, you are the one account
that will not balance, will not answer back.

I pitched myself to you like Series A,
all upside, vision, terminal growth curve.
You smiled a polite *non merci* and turned,
your *sang-froid* colder than I could deserve.

I wanted *folie à deux*—our shared delusion,
two founders mad enough to bet the farm.
Instead I'm sole proprietor of longing,
a startup burning cash to fund your charm.

At 3 a.m. I draft you *roman à clef*,
disguise your name in emails I don't send,
rebrand my desperation as a strategy,
call it *rapport*, call it *means to an end*.

You are the market I cannot corner,
the exit that keeps slipping past the close.
I offer everything—my restless genius—
you counter with a shrug, a *comme ci, comme ça* pose.

Deliver it, then. Give me the *coup de grâce*,
the mercy-blow that ends this bleeding pitch.
I've optimized for everything but this:
the *no* that leaves me infinitely rich

in wanting. *C'est la vie*, the analysts would say.
But I don't scale. I don't diversify my ache.
I'm liquidating slowly, *tête-à-tête*
with an empty chair, still hungry, still awake—

still building castles, *châteaux en Espagne*,
where you say *oui* and mean it, where we merge.
The morning comes. I straighten my *cravate*.
Another quarter. Another restless surge.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
